newsitem.title: GERMANY: STRONGER DMK MAKES BUNDS RESILIENT IN LATE TRADE.
newsitem.headline: STRONGER DMK MAKES BUNDS RESILIENT IN LATE TRADE.

text.p: German Bunds showed resilience in the face of a steep fall in U.S. Treasuries on Friday, buoyed by the appreciation of the mark against the dollar and a steepening of the German yield curve following comments from Bundesbank council member in the morning.
September Bunds were quoted at 101.92 at 1445 GMT, down 18 basis points from Thursday's close, after trading in a range of 101.62 to 102.11.
"We'd be much weaker if it weren't for the strengthening mark," one Bund dealer said.
U.S. Treasuries fell sharply on Friday amid deteriorated technical conditions, continuing a decline which set in on Thursday.

The dollar fell to just above 1.85 marks, hit by heavy sterling sales and by pre-weekend profit-taking, dampening fears that the Bundesbank may raise money market rates next week to stem the recent slide of the mark.

The short end of the German debt market gained support after Welteke said in a radio that while there was a danger of imported inflation "it is not appropriate to turn the interest rate screw" due to slow growth and high unemployment.
But Welteke also said that the Bundesbank had already signalled when the mark was at 1.70 to the dollar that the previous long-term correction of the mark was over.
All eyes are now on Tuesday, when the Bundesbank is due to set its weekly repo tender and signal whether it wants money market interest rates to remain unchanged or to rise.
Call money rates stayed firm at around 3.15 percent amid speculation that the Bundesbank may signal higher rates.
